correctness.rationale: PASS for the final repaired claim. Frozen Step 4 has a real proof gap: when ε_p=1, knowing m−1 distinct smooth roots and degree m does not force the remaining multiplicity to occur at a=2; a known smooth root could repeat. This does not make the statement false. The complete replacement proof and corresponding reproducibility notes are in /workspace/repairs/1/RESULT.md and VERIFICATION.md. On re-audit, in u=X²,y=Y²,z=Z² the target takes [u^{p−1}y^mz^m] of (u²+bu+c)^{p−1}. For formal roots r,s, its middle u coefficient is ∑r^js^{p−1−j}=(r−s)^{p−1}=(b²−4c)^m by the characteristic-p binomial identity. The discriminant is (a−2)((a+2)(y+z)²−4yz). Extracting [y^mz^m] and using binom(2j,j)=(−4)^j binom(m,j) in F_p gives (a−2)^m(−4)^m H_m(a+2). Vandermonde yields H_m(1−t)=(−1)^mH_m(t); 4^m=1, yielding exactly the claimed normalized coefficient on all of A¹, without inverting any boundary parameter. The plane Čech calculation uses F_a^{p−1}, even exponents kill the off-diagonal terms, and permutation symmetry gives the scalar. The derivative equations give precisely 2,−2,−1 as singular. H_m(0)=1 and H_m(1)=(−1)^m; the classical distinct F_{p²} roots give m−ε_p smooth zeros and exactly m+ε_p at 2. In characteristic seven H_3(−3)=28, giving multiplicity four. Frobenius is invertible or zero on the smooth genus-three H¹, so its stable rank and the Cartier kernel give the asserted p-rank and a-number; cubing triples the boundary order. The frozen verification file and unchanged verify_extended_hasse.py were inspected: the reported script compares three coefficient vectors at p=5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29; uploaded code was not run and the uniform proof is independent of those finite samples. No Lean or expert attestation is asserted.
